I am a 50-year-old woman who has farmed the land in Quzhou County my whole life. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain, and I know this soil well. Here, everyone grows the wheat-maize rotation — it is the only system that reliably feeds our family and brings in cash. I will stick with what works.

This autumn, I will sow **winter wheat** on all 8 mu. I will use **Luyuan 502**, an improved variety that my neighbours have had good results with — it stands up well and yields steadily. Before sowing in early October, I will do **rotary tillage** to break up the stubble from the previous maize crop and prepare a fine seedbed. For the wheat, I will apply a basal compound fertilizer at about 100 kg per mu, and topdress with urea so the total nitrogen reaches about **50 kg per mu**. I will also get about **15 kg P₂O₅** and **10 kg K₂O** per mu from the compound fertilizer. The wheat will need **three irrigations** — one at sowing if it is dry, one at jointing in spring, and one at grain filling. I will spray pesticides **three times**: herbicide once after sowing, and then insecticide and fungicide each once in spring when the pests and diseases start.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant **summer maize** on the same 8 mu. I will sow **Deng hai 605**, a hybrid maize seed that gives high yields and matures quickly enough for the short summer season. Most farmers here, including me, use **no-tillage** for maize — we just sow directly into the wheat stubble to save time, labour, and fuel. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat, so I will apply about **20 kg nitrogen per mu**, plus **10 kg P₂O₅** and **5 kg K₂O**. I will irrigate **twice** — once if the soil is dry at sowing, and again at the big喇叭口 stage or tasselling. For pesticides, I will spray **three times** total: herbicide once, and insecticide twice to control corn borers and aphids.

This double-cropping system is hard work, but it is what our land and climate are made for. I expect about **1,000 jin per mu** (1,000 kg) from the wheat and about **1,100 jin per mu** (1,100 kg) from the maize.

decision.reasoning_summary: I have farmed in Quzhou County for decades and know that the wheat-maize double-cropping rotation is the most reliable and profitable system on the North China Plain. With about 8 mu of land, I will grow improved Luyuan 502 wheat in winter and hybrid Deng hai 605 maize in summer, matching what successful neighbouring households do. Wheat requires rotary tillage and more intensive inputs including three irrigations and higher nitrogen, while maize is typically no-tilled directly into wheat stubble with lighter fertilizer and two irrigations, saving labour during the busy summer season.
